summary.title: API design guide | Cloud API Design Guide
summary.one_liner: Google's internal-origin guide to designing networked REST and gRPC APIs, which mostly points to the numbered AIP standards for specific rules.
keywords: how to design a networked api
takeaways: Google has used this general design guide internally since 2014 for Cloud APIs and other Google APIs.
The guide applies to both REST and RPC APIs, with a particular focus on gRPC APIs defined with Protocol Buffers.
Topics such as resource-oriented design, resource names, and standard methods (Get, List, Create, Update, Delete) are covered in linked AIPs (AIP-121, AIP-122, AIP-131 to AIP-135).
Custom methods, standard fields, errors, versioning, and backward compatibility are addressed by further AIPs referenced from the guide.
Cloud Endpoints developers are strongly encouraged to follow these principles, though use is not mandated.
summary.summary: This page is the introduction and index for Google's API Design Guide, a general guide for networked APIs used inside Google since 2014. It explains that the guide covers both REST and RPC APIs, with focus on gRPC APIs using Protocol Buffers and API Service Configuration for HTTP mapping. The page mostly serves as a table of contents, pointing each topic (resource design, naming, standard and custom methods, fields, errors, versioning, backward compatibility, naming conventions) to a specific AIP. It also notes the guide is a living document using RFC 2119 requirement keywords.
